_readme: English text overlay for torque-data.json. Loaded by en/torque.html on top of ../torque-data.json.
This file holds NO torque figures. Values, units, fits, sources and cross-checks all stay in torque-data.json,
so the English page can never drift away from the Japanese one on the numbers.
items[<id>].aliases       -> PREPENDED to item.aliases (the Japanese aliases stay searchable)
items[<id>].notes         -> replaces item.notes wholesale (same length as the Japanese array)
items[<id>].procedure     -> replaces item.procedure ('\n' is rendered as a line break)
items[<id>].cross_notes   -> keyed by the index in item.cross
for_version must match torque-data.json's version. If it does not, the page still works but logs a warning:
the Japanese text shows through wherever this file has no entry, which is the safe failure mode.
An Italian page needs only a copy of this file with the strings translated - no second copy of the data.
target: FIAT 500 / FIAT 126 (filtered by engine family and base body)

oem.label: Fiat factory repair manual "Neuer 500 und 500 D" (German)

e500.label: 500-series engine
e500.note: Figures come from the Fiat factory manual (German, 110 / 110D) and the Autobooks English workshop manual (1957-73). The Giardiniera's 120.000 is given the same figures because the engine table in the factory supplement has the same layout and the same part numbers as the 110D - only the tightening-sequence diagram differs.

e126.label: 126-series engine
e126.note: Figures come from the 126 Autobook (594 cc, 126 A.000) and have been checked entry by entry against the Bucheli manual (652 cc, 126 A1). The 126 A5.000 fitted to the Nuova 500 R differs in camshaft, carburetter, output and dynamo, but no difference in tightening torque appears in the sources (Fiat "500 VARIANTI" 603.91.687).

cautions: When screwing into aluminium or cast iron, use less than these figures - otherwise the threads pull out
Oil or grease on the threads raises the clamping force by 20-30% at the same torque, which means overtightening
Fine threads (M12x1.25 and similar) take slightly more than coarse threads
On rusted or galled threads most of the torque is lost to friction and never becomes clamping force

_refs_readme: Where a source points to a page in the printed book, the Japanese data writes it as "本 pNN" (book, not PDF page) and "本文" (in the running text, not in a table). These are looked up by exact string and applied to item.source_id, cross[].ref and sequences[].ref. Anything not listed here ("p22", "FIG 1:44") is already language-neutral and passes through unchanged.

refs.p22 エキゾーストマニホールド→シリンダーヘッド: p22, exhaust manifold to cylinder head

cylinder-head-nut.name: Cylinder head nuts
notes: Always work in the correct diagonal sequence
Tightening in two stages is recommended (first pass 25 N·m = 2.5 kgf·m / 18.1 lb·ft, then the final figure)
The sequence diagram differs by engine type: FIG 1:44 for the Nuova 500 N, FIG 1:46 for the 500 D / F / L and the Giardiniera (English WSM). The torque figure is the same for all of them.

rocker-shaft-support.name: Rocker shaft support nuts
notes: Always reset the valve clearances after refitting

main-bearing-carrier.name: Main bearing carrier bolts
notes: The bolts holding the body that carries the crankshaft main bearing shells.

This line appears only in the tightening-torque table of the German factory manual; the English WSM has no matching entry. Figures that are not printed in a source are never created by conversion, so no lb·ft is given.

conrod-cap.name: Big-end (connecting rod) cap nuts
notes: Check the bearing clearance with Plastigauge (specified 0.011-0.061 mm)

flywheel-bolt.name: Flywheel bolts
notes: Use a new lock plate and bend the tabs over after tightening
Check the alignment marks against the crankshaft before fitting

centrifugal-filter-bolt.name: Centrifugal oil filter hollow bolt
notes: A very high torque. It cannot be reached without a locking tool
Check that the O-ring is correctly seated before tightening

camshaft-sprocket.name: Camshaft gear bolt
notes: The same point on the 126 (594 / 652 cc) is 1.0 kgf·m = 10 N·m, which falls right between the two figures.

cross_notes.1: Only the German factory manual gives the higher 1.1 kgf·m = 11 N·m. The English WSM (6.5 lb·ft, about 8.8 N·m) and Haynes p22 (0.9 kgf·m = 8.8 N·m) agree with each other, so this page takes 0.9 kgf·m as the main figure.

centrifugal-filter-cover.name: Centrifugal oil filter cover bolts
notes: Not the same thing as the hollow bolt (15.0 kgf·m). Mixing the two up will wreck the part

generator-pulley-nut.name: Dynamo pulley nut
notes: Belt tension is set by the number of split shims (remove shims to tighten the belt, add them to slacken it)
About 10 mm of deflection under a 10 kg push at mid-span is correct
The English WSM gives the pulley and the fan nut the same 14.5 lb·ft, but the German factory manual lists the fan side separately at 3.5 kgf·m = 34 N·m. See the separate entry for the fan nut.

generator-bearing-stop.name: Dynamo commutator-end bearing outer race retainer nut
notes: A tiny torque, only touched when the dynamo is stripped. At around 1 N·m it is below the range of most torque wrenches.
Printed only in the English WSM. Figures not in a source are not created by conversion, so no kgf·m is given.

generator-fan-nut.name: Cooling fan to dynamo nut
notes: The same point on the 126 (594 / 652 cc) is also 3.5 kgf·m = 34 N·m, agreeing with the German factory manual.

cross_notes.1: The English WSM covers the pulley and the fan in a single line at 14.5 lb·ft, about 20 N·m. The German factory manual lists the fan nut on its own at 3.5 kgf·m = 34 N·m, and both 126 manuals agree with the 3.5 kgf·m figure.

spark-plug.name: Spark plugs
notes: Anti-seize compound on the threads is recommended
Specified electrode gap 0.48-0.58 mm

clutch-cover.name: Clutch cover (pressure plate) bolts
notes: Tighten a little at a time in a diagonal sequence
Take care not to overtighten - the figure is lower than it looks
Use of the centring tool (A.62023) is recommended

gearbox-to-engine.name: Clutch housing to engine nuts
notes: The factory manual reads "Mutter zur Befestigung des Kupplungsgehäuses am Motor" - the nuts holding the clutch housing to the engine, not to the body.

diff-bearing-cap.name: Differential bearing cap nuts
notes: Specified crownwheel-to-pinion backlash 0.08-0.12 mm

diff-rolling-torque.name: Differential bearing preload (rolling resistance)
notes: Do not mistake this figure for a tightening torque.
diff-rolling-torque.procedure: This is not a torque-wrench setting. Use the adjusters until the resistance felt when turning the differential is 1.37 ± 0.09 N·m (1.01 ± 0.07 lb·ft).

crown-wheel-bolt.name: Crownwheel (ring gear) bolts
notes: Use a new lock plate and bend the tabs over after tightening.

starter-motor.name: Starter motor mounting nuts
notes: It bolts to the clutch housing, so the figure still applies as a body-side value even if the engine has been changed.
Printed only in the English WSM; the German factory manual has no matching line. Figures not in a source are not created by conversion, so no kgf·m is given.

wheel-bolt.name: Road wheel bolts
notes: Tighten in a diagonal sequence
Always re-check them after driving
Aftermarket wheels with a different seat shape may not clamp properly even at the specified figure

rear-swingarm-pivot.name: Rear swinging arm pivot pin nut

rear-outer-support.name: Rear outer support fixing screws
notes: Rear toe-in is set here (tolerance 0°10')

rear-hub-bearing.name: Rear wheel bearing (wheel shaft nut)
notes: Pack the bearing with Fiat MR grease
rear-hub-bearing.procedure: Not tightened to a fixed torque - set by rolling resistance. Tighten the nut progressively and stop as soon as the turning resistance reaches 0.5 N·m (0.05 kgf·m / 0.36 lb·ft). If the resistance is too high, fit a new elastic spacer.

front-swingarm-hub-nut.name: Front swinging arm to hub assembly nut
notes: The upper limit comes from the factory manual, 59 N·m (6.0 kgf·m). The English WSM prints only the single figure 39.8 lb·ft (54 N·m), so the lb·ft column is left as the single figure in the source - no upper limit is invented by conversion.

leaf-spring-kingpin.name: Leaf spring to king pin housing

front-swingarm-pin-body.name: Front swinging arm pin to body

front-hub-nut.name: Front hub nut (bearing adjustment)
notes: Aim for a final hub end float of 0.025-0.10 mm
Overtightening will burn the bearing out
front-hub-nut.procedure:
Do not simply leave it tight - tighten, then back off. The method depends on the type of hub.
[Split pin type] Tighten to 29 N·m (3.0 kgf·m / 21.7 lb·ft), then back off 60° (one flat of the hexagon).
[Staked type] Tighten to 20 N·m (2.0 kgf·m / 14.5 lb·ft) to bed the bearing in, then slacken off. Re-tighten to 6.9 N·m (0.7 kgf·m / 5.1 lb·ft) and back off 30° from there.

brake-backplate-front.name: Brake backplate to king pin housing (front)
notes: Thread size M8x1.25.
The source is the German factory manual, which prints kgf·m only. The English WSM has no matching entry, so no lb·ft is shown.

brake-backplate-rear.name: Brake backplate to trailing arm (rear)
notes: Thread size M10x1.25. At the rear this also clamps the bearing flange.
The lb·ft figure is converted from kgf·m (no matching entry in the English WSM).
The source is the German factory manual, which prints kgf·m only. The English WSM has no matching entry, so no lb·ft is shown.

pitman-arm-nut.name: Pitman (drop) arm nut
notes: One of the highest torques on this page
The upper limit comes from the factory manual, 108 N·m (11.0 kgf·m). The English WSM prints only the single figure 72 lb·ft (98 N·m), so the lb·ft column is left as the single figure in the source.

tie-rod-ball-pin.name: Track rod end ball pin nut
notes: Front toe-in is 0-2 mm (measured at the wheel rims)

relay-lever-pivot.name: Relay lever pivot pin nut
notes: The English WSM gives this point twice: 39-43 lb·ft (53-58 N·m) on p94 and 78-85 lb·ft (106-115 N·m) on p95. The p94 figure agrees with the factory manual's 5500-6000 mmkg = 5.5-6.0 kgf·m (54-59 N·m) and has been adopted.

relay-lever-support.name: Relay lever support to body
notes: The bolts holding the support to the body. The figure differs from the relay lever pin itself (a separate entry) - do not mix the two up.

Printed only in the English WSM; the table in the German factory manual (p179) has just five steering lines and no entry for this. Figures not in a source are not created by conversion, so no kgf·m is given.

steering-wheel-nut.name: Steering wheel nut
notes: If the steering wheel comes loose you lose all steering. Always re-tighten to the specified figure after removal.

oil-drain.name: Engine oil drain plug
notes: Renew the washer every time
The thread is in aluminium - never overtighten

rocker-cover.name: Rocker cover (tappet cover)
notes: Overtightening crushes the gasket and makes the leak worse

exhaust-manifold.name: Exhaust manifold / silencer
notes: It works loose with heat - re-tighten after a short run
The figure is for the manifold to the cylinder head. The source prints kgf·m only (2.5 kgf·m = 24.5 N·m); figures not in a source are not created by conversion, so no lb·ft is shown.
Haynes is the only source with a figure for this point; the English WSM, the German factory manual and both 126 manuals have no matching line.

engine-mount.name: Engine mountings
notes: Do the final tightening with the weight of the car on the mountings, so no twist is left in the rubber
engine-mount.no_spec_note: There is no single figure for the mounting as a whole, but each fixing point has one. 500: see the separate entry "Power unit lower mounting nuts (body side)", 24.5-29.4 N·m (18.1-21.7 lb·ft). 126: the five "Engine mounting: ..." entries.

powerplant-mount-lower.name: Power unit lower mounting nuts (body side)
notes: The four lower fixings holding the gearbox and differential to the body. Fit the front support screws finger tight first and do the final tightening last.
Printed only in the English WSM. Figures not in a source are not created by conversion, so no kgf·m is given.

carburettor.name: Carburetter mounting nuts
notes: Overtightening distorts the flange and lets it draw air
Work alternately from side to side, a little at a time

intake-manifold.name: Inlet manifold
notes: A common source of air leaks

brake-pipe.name: Brake pipe flare nuts
notes: Overtightening crushes the flare and makes the leak worse
Always press the pedal and check for leaks afterwards
brake-pipe.no_spec_note: No figure in the sources. The English WSM describes how to disconnect the hose (book p101) but gives no torque for the flare nut.

wheel-cylinder.name: Wheel cylinder mounting
notes: Lining wear limit 1.5 mm; drums may be skimmed to standard +1.0 mm
wheel-cylinder.no_spec_note: The 126 (652 cc, Bucheli) specifies 9.8 N·m (1.0 kgf·m), listed on this page as the separate entry "Wheel cylinder mounting bolts". Whether the 500 uses the same figure has not been confirmed.

master-cylinder.name: Master cylinder mounting
master-cylinder.no_spec_note: The 126 (652 cc, Bucheli) specifies 14.7 N·m (1.5 kgf·m), listed on this page as the separate entry "Master cylinder to pedal bracket". Whether the 500 uses the same figure has not been confirmed.

seat-belt-anchor.name: Seat belt anchorages
notes: If the body panel is too thin, add a spreader plate behind it
seat-belt-anchor.no_spec_note: Seat belts were not standard equipment at the time, so the manuals have no entry at all (the English WSM only mentions detaching the seat belt mountings from the floor, book p102). As a retrofit part, follow the figure supplied with the fitting kit.

door-hinge.name: Door hinges
notes: Set the door fit with the bolts finger tight, then tighten fully

cylinder-head-nut-126.name: Cylinder head nuts
notes: The cap nuts take the same 39 N·m (4.0 kgf·m).
Tighten in the order shown in FIG 1:5. Tighten cold and re-check after the specified running-in period.

camshaft-sprocket-126.name: Camshaft sprocket bolt
notes: A low figure - take care not to overtighten.

engine-pulley-bolt-126.name: Engine pulley centre bolt (centrifugal oil filter)
notes: A very high torque. Lock the flywheel to stop the crankshaft turning.

spark-plug-126.name: Spark plugs
notes: The manual states it as a maximum: do not exceed 29 N·m (3.0 kgf·m / 22 lb·ft).
Specified plugs: Marelli CW 8 NP / Champion L 81 Y.

mount-rubber-crossmember-126.name: Engine mounting: rubber mount to crossmember
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual. The 594 cc sources have no matching figure.

mount-crossmember-body-126.name: Engine mounting: crossmember to body
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

mount-rubber-gearbox-126.name: Engine mounting: rubber mount to gearbox casing
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

mount-bracket-rear-crossmember-126.name: Engine mounting: bracket to rear crossmember
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

mount-bracket-powerplant-126.name: Engine mounting: bracket to power unit
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

clutch-release-fork-126.name: Clutch release fork fixing
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

clutch-pedal-shaft-126.name: Clutch / brake pedal shaft nut
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

bellhousing-to-engine-126.name: Clutch housing to engine nuts
notes: Bucheli gives this point twice, once as 25 N·m (2.5 kgf·m) and once as 25-34 N·m (2.5-3.5 kgf·m). The 25 N·m (2.5 kgf·m) figure, which agrees with the Autobook table, has been adopted.

gearbox-to-bellhousing-126.name: Gearbox casing to clutch housing nuts

gearbox-layshaft-126.name: Gearbox layshaft (countershaft) nut
notes: After reaching the specified torque, keep tightening until the split pin holes line up - never slacken back.
Always use a new split pin.

gearbox-mainshaft-126.name: Gearbox mainshaft nut
notes: After reaching the specified torque, keep tightening until the split pin holes line up - never slacken back.
Always use a new split pin.

crown-wheel-bolt-126.name: Crownwheel (ring gear) bolts
notes: The 500 uses 31 N·m (3.2 kgf·m) - a different figure. Make sure you have the right base body selected.

diff-bearing-housing-126.name: Differential bearing housing nuts
notes: The 500's differential bearing cap (37 N·m = 3.8 kgf·m) differs in both design and figure.

diff-rolling-torque-126.name: Differential bearing preload (rolling resistance)
notes: Do not mistake this figure for a tightening torque.
diff-rolling-torque-126.procedure: Not a torque-wrench setting - it is set with shims. Choose shims so that the differential on its own turns with 1.3-1.5 N·m (13-15 kgf·cm) of resistance, and 2.0-4.9 N·m (20-50 kgf·cm) with the crownwheel fitted.

wheel-bolt-126.name: Road wheel bolts
notes: The same figure front and rear. Tighten diagonally, a little at a time, over several passes.

cross_notes.0: The 652 cc Bucheli gives 69 N·m (7.0 kgf·m), 40% higher than the 594 cc Autobook. Haynes 126 p89 gives 36 lb·ft / 50 N·m = 5.0 kgf·m, agreeing with the Autobook, as does the table on the FD Ricambi site (49 N·m = 5.0 kgf·m). This page takes 5.0 kgf·m as the main figure, but check the year of the car and the size of the wheel bolts before deciding.

leaf-spring-kingpin-126.name: Leaf spring to king pin housing nut

control-arm-shaft-126.name: Front control arm to shaft nut

cross_notes.0: Only the 652 cc Bucheli gives the higher 49 N·m (5.0 kgf·m). The 594 cc Autobook (29 N·m = 3.0 kgf·m) and Haynes 126 p89 (22 lb·ft / 30 N·m = 3.0 kgf·m) agree with each other, so this page takes 3.0 kgf·m as the main figure.

control-arm-shaft-body-126.name: Front control arm shaft to body nuts

cross_notes.0: Only the 652 cc Bucheli gives the higher 49 N·m (5.0 kgf·m). The 594 cc Autobook (29 N·m = 3.0 kgf·m) and Haynes 126 p89 (22 lb·ft / 30 N·m = 3.0 kgf·m) agree with each other, so this page takes 3.0 kgf·m as the main figure.

control-arm-knuckle-126.name: Front control arm to king pin housing nut

cross_notes.0: The 652 cc Bucheli gives 69 N·m (7.0 kgf·m) for a self-locking nut. A different type of nut may be involved, but the 594 cc Autobook (59 N·m = 6.0 kgf·m) and Haynes 126 p89 (44 lb·ft / 61 N·m = 6.0 kgf·m) agree with each other, so this page takes 6.0 kgf·m as the main figure.

front-damper-126.name: Front damper (shock absorber) upper and lower nuts

front-hub-nut-126.name: Front hub nut (bearing adjustment)
notes: Do not just tighten to the number - you will destroy the bearing.
Bucheli also prints an equally low 4.9 N·m (0.5 kgf·m); both sources agree that this is a tighten-then-back-off procedure.
front-hub-nut-126.procedure: Not left at the specified torque. Tighten to 6.9 N·m (0.7 kgf·m / 5 lb·ft) to bed the bearing in, then back off about 30° and fit the split pin.

brake-backplate-front-126.name: Brake backplate to king pin housing (front)
notes: Bucheli lists this point twice - 29 N·m (3.0 kgf·m) in the suspension table and 20 N·m (2.0 kgf·m) in the brake table. The brake table figure of 20 N·m (2.0 kgf·m), which agrees with the Autobook, has been adopted.

rear-arm-support-front-126.name: Rear trailing arm front support bolts

rear-damper-126.name: Rear damper (shock absorber) upper and lower nuts

rear-hub-bearing-126.name: Rear wheel bearing (hub nut)
notes: Re-using the spacer will not give the specified preload.
Printing a large figure here would invite accidents - follow the procedure instead.
rear-hub-bearing-126.procedure: Controlled by rolling resistance, not by a fixed torque. Always fit a new spacer (collar) on assembly, use the specified grease (Fiat MR 3) and tighten until the specified rolling resistance is reached.

steering-wheel-nut-126.name: Steering wheel nut
notes: Stake the nut after tightening to lock it.

steering-column-support-126.name: Steering column upper rear mounting nuts

pitman-arm-nut-126.name: Pitman (drop) arm nut
notes: The 500 is also 98-108 N·m (10.0-11.0 kgf·m) - the same order of magnitude.

cross_notes.0: Bucheli writes "Lenkhebelbefestigungsmutter 10", which reads as 9.8 N·m (1.0 kgf·m), but the 594 cc Autobook gives 98 N·m (10 kgf·m / 72 lb·ft) and the 500 is 98-108 N·m (10-11 kgf·m). The Bucheli figure has been judged a misprint with the decimal point dropped - 9.8 N·m would be nowhere near tight enough. Haynes 126 p89 also gives "Drop arm nut 72 lb·ft / 100 N·m" = 10.0 kgf·m, confirming the misprint with a third source. The table on the FD Ricambi site reproduces Bucheli's "10" unchanged.

tie-rod-clamp-126.name: Track rod clamp (adjusting sleeve) nuts
notes: Tighten after setting the toe.

ball-joint-stud-126.name: Track rod end ball joint nut
notes: Fit a new split pin.

wheel-cylinder-126.name: Wheel cylinder mounting bolts
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual. A low figure - take care not to overtighten.

brake-hose-union-126.name: Brake hose union (wheel cylinder end)
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.

handbrake-lever-126.name: Handbrake lever mounting
notes: Printed only in the 652 cc manual.
